purpose: Test whether the frozen kinetic-gate dynamic-range theorem has a paper-anchored derivation, distinguish it from the closest published theories, and add exact functional-family benchmarks without promoting the action to an observationally successful theory.

source_or_paper_gate.rule: A new builder or theorem promotion requires an existing real dataset or primary paper/analytic benchmark that can falsify its implementation. A genuinely new formula need not already appear in a paper, but its inputs, dimensions, known limits, and closest control must be paper-anchored.
source_or_paper_gate.formalism_anchor: arXiv:0806.0336 equations 45 and 48 give the constraint-reduced kinetic matrix K_IJ=P_<IJ>+2 P_<MJ>,<IK> X^MK and spatial-gradient matrix P_<IJ> for general P(X^IJ,phi^K).

theorem_slice.action: P=P0(X)+Z(u)Y with u=beta X^2, X>0, beta>0, Z>0 and C2
theorem_slice.definitions: q=d ln Z/d ln u; M=Z(Z_X+2 X Z_XX)-4 X Z_X^2
theorem_slice.scope: Necessary sign condition for one active aligned-timelike two-field mixing contribution; not a full-action no-go, not a causality theorem, and not observational evidence.

analytic_benchmarks.expected: The published K_IJ and gradient matrices specialize exactly to the predecessor two-field principal block.
For alpha,p>0, M>=0 iff q=alpha p u^p<=p-1/4, which is impossible for p<=1/4 and finite-range for p>1/4.
For p>0, q=p and M=-(2 Z^2/X)(p+4p^2)<0 everywhere.
The equality solution reaches a pole exactly at U/u0=[1+1/(4q0)]^4, showing the comparison bound is sharp within the scalar inequality.
q=M=0; the growing-gate hypothesis is absent and the theorem does not apply.

primary_literature.overlap: Two-field kinetic coupling depends on a scalar field, not the derivative invariant X.

primary_literature.overlap: Published characteristic-speed breakdown; neighboring pathology, not the two-field logarithmic-slope inequality.

primary_literature.overlap: UV/positivity constraints on kinetic screening, distinct from the active two-field mixing bound.

primary_literature.title: Perturbations and stability conditions of k-essence and kinetic gravity braiding models in two-field measure theory

primary_literature.class: two-field metric depending on the fields
primary_literature.overlap: Closest modern two-field kinetic-metric analysis; its metric is G_IJ(phi), not G_IJ(X).

primary_literature.title: A novel two-field pure K-essence for inflation, dark matter, dark energy and black holes
primary_literature.overlap: Closest published action envelope; studies quotient families and background/perturbation examples rather than the separable Z(x)y finite-range theorem.

primary_literature.title: Multi-Field Dilaton Screening Beyond the Thin-Shell Mechanism
primary_literature.overlap: Closest current screening application with a second-field gradient and a kinetic prefactor. Its prefactor is field-dependent W(chi), and its static charge/energy analysis does not state the derivative-invariant Z(X) logarithmic-slope finite-range theorem.
